name: Edge Transition
description: The boundary of the playfield as a door rather than a wall. It owns which edges are exits and what lies beyond each one — and only that. Walking off the north edge can lead somewhere GENERATED, where the destination is a fresh seed and the world is different every time, or somewhere AUTHORED, where the edge names a destination that is the same on every visit and can be hand-tuned; a route that alternates the two is how an overworld gets a designed spine with wilderness between its vertebrae. It deliberately does not own seeds: world.run_seed_manager issues those, and a build with one should hand this its stream rather than letting two components invent numbers. It does not own room topology either — world.interconnected_map_graph owns rooms, edges and gates, and an authored destination here is a room id that graph can resolve. And it does not move anybody: it reports that a boundary was crossed and where that leads, and whoever owns the world acts on it.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: exitEdges
inputs.description: Which boundaries are doors. An edge left out is a wall, which is how a level fences one side without fencing all four.

inputs.name: destinations
inputs.description: Authored exits, keyed by edge: {"north": {"id": "cave", "seed": 4242}}. An edge named here always leads to the same place; an edge absent from it is generated. Both may be present at once.

inputs.name: requireStandingAtEdge
inputs.description: Whether the crossing must start from a tile on the boundary itself. True means a player walks to the edge and then presses onward, which is the readable gesture; false lets anything that reports a blocked move at the border trigger it.

inputs.name: cooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Quiet period after a crossing. Held movement keys repeat, and without this the first frame of the next region immediately crosses back.

outputs.name: currentDestination
outputs.description: Where the last crossing led: {edge, id, seed, generated}. Null before the first.

provenance: Requested from play: walking off a green edge tile should lead somewhere, sometimes generated and sometimes authored.
